title: Comelec targets 4 million new voters for 2028 elections

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) expects four million new voter registrants for the 2028 elections, exceeding its earlier target.
Comelec Chair George Erwin Garcia made the estimate on Sunday, following the resumption of voter registration on Nov. 10. The poll body will accept applications until July 30, 2027.
Garcia earlier said the Comelec was targeting three million new voter registrants for the 2028 elections, raising the country’s registered voters from 71 million to 74 million by 2028.
“We believe this will exceed our estimate of 3 million [new voter registrants], and we might reach around 4 million,” Garcia said in an interview with dzBB.

“That’s good news because 2028 will be a very crucial, critical, and important election in our country, as we will elect a new president and vice president and fill other national and local positions,” he added.

Garcia also welcomed the high turnout of voter registrants since the resumption of registration, describing it as a “blockbuster.” He said the poll body had received around 140,000 to 150,000 applications so far.
Many of those who lined up on the first day of the resumed voter registration were young Filipinos. Garcia earlier described the youth turnout as a “good indication.”
Interested voter registrants can submit their applications through the local offices of their respective election officers, satellite or mall registration sites, and the Register Anywhere Program.

To register as a voter, an individual must be at least 18 years old on or before election day on May 8, 2028. They must also have resided in the Philippines for at least one year and in the place where they intend to vote for at least six months immediately preceding the elections.
An applicant must present any of the following valid IDs, along with a photocopy:

items: Student ID or library card signed by a school authority
Social Security System or Government Service Insurance System ID, or other Unified Multi-Purpose ID
Integrated Bar of the Philippines ID card
Certificate of Confirmation issued by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, for members of Indigenous Cultural Communities or Indigenous Peoples
Other valid government-issued IDs that meet Comelec’s requirements
